original_question: Is there a universal extension of the Kontsevich construction from affine Poisson manifolds to the commutative but non-associative calculus of cyclic words with pair-of-pants multiplication in formal noncommutative or super-geometry, such that it remains well defined for the full family of graph-encoded symmetries Q∈sym([[P,P]]=0) of Poisson structures?
target_in_paper: Section 8.2, Problem 20: the paper asks whether the Kontsevich construction on finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds has a well-defined generalization to the cyclic-word calculus of formal noncommutative (super)geometry, uniformly for graph-encoded Poisson symmetries Q(P) in sym([[P,P]] = 0). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the paper-faithful content: the source setting is affine Poisson manifolds, the target setting is the commutative non-associative calculus of cyclic words, the pair-of-pants multiplication is part of the target structure, the framework is Kontsevich formal noncommutative (super)geometry, and the universality requirement is with respect to graph-encoded symmetries Q in sym([[P,P]] = 0). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))
missing_details: The exact target is not a broad universal extension question in general, but specifically Problem 20 in Section 8.2, i.e. in the paper's quantization discussion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))

To make the question fully stand-alone, the source construction should be identified as the Kontsevich deformation-quantization construction, originally defined for finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds (M_aff, P) with dim M_aff < infinity. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))

The symbols should be unpacked: P denotes a classical Poisson bivector, and Q(P) in sym([[P,P]] = 0) means an infinitesimal symmetry of the Jacobi identity for Poisson bivectors. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))

The paper's graph-encoded symmetries are those produced from graph cocycles via the orientation morphism, so that suitable gamma in ker[bullet-bullet, .] are sent to Poisson cocycles Q(P) = O_r(gamma)(P). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))

The target algebraic structure is stated more precisely as the calculus of cyclic words equipped with the topological pair-of-pants multiplication S^1 x S^1 -> S^1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))

The nearby context notes that the deformation-quantization construction is essentially indifferent to choosing the real or complex field, but Problem 20 itself does not impose any extra ambient-field restriction. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))

There are no additional homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'for sufficiently large' hypotheses in Problem 20; adding any such restriction would move away from the paper's actual scope. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))

The paper's emphasis is first on well-definedness and then on universality with respect to the set of graph-encoded symmetries; stating only existence understates that requirement. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))
refined_question: Does the Kontsevich deformation-quantization construction, originally defined for every finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifold (M_aff, P), admit a well-defined generalization to the commutative, non-associative calculus of cyclic words equipped with the topological pair-of-pants multiplication S^1 x S^1 -> S^1 in Kontsevich formal noncommutative (super)geometry, in a way that is universal with respect to the graph-encoded infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) in sym([[P,P]] = 0) of Poisson structures P? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))
justification: This draft is aimed at Problem 20, not at the earlier graph-cohomology, globalization, or BV-quantization problems. The identifying phrases cyclic words, pair-of-pants multiplication, formal noncommutative (super)geometry, and universality with respect to graph-encoded symmetries Q in sym([[P,P]] = 0) occur together only in Problem 20. The Introduction supplies the meaning of Q, the universality condition, and the finite-dimensional affine Poisson-manifold setting, while Section 8.2 identifies the underlying Kontsevich construction as deformation quantization and notes the real/complex-field indifference of that construction. The paper does not state an equivalent reformulation of Problem 20. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05844))
